body.translated_text: <s>Sūtrārthasamuccayopadeśa</s> (Instruction on the Compendium of Sūtra Meanings)

children.translated_text: Having perceived the profound, noble sūtra-matrix (<s>mātṛkā</s>), comparable to the ocean and space,
I write down the meanings arisen from the mouth of the illustrious <s>Guru</s> — difficult to obtain. // 1 //

body.text: atra bodhisattvānāṃ ratnopamāḥ pañcāśad dharmāḥ prāṇopamādayaḥ / tān abhidhāsye kiñcit / tadyathā-
body.translated_text: Here, fifty qualities comparable to jewels belong to <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, beginning with those comparable to the breath of life (<s>prāṇa</s>). I shall briefly explain them. They are as follows:
Life-span is the support of warmth and consciousness. // 2ab //

body.text: yathā sattvāḥ prāṇeṣu snihyantaḥ prāṇāṃścāśrayante, tathā bodhisattvā api prāṇopamabodhicitte snihyantastadāśrayante / mātāpitṛsamo dharmastu śūnyatā-karuṇe / tadanotpāde na bodhisattvasambhavaḥ / gṛhiṇīvat mṛti-śikṣā-karmaṇisaṃcitisaṃjñāni ahorātraṃ triḥ samāgamaḥ / gṛhavad daśa kuśalāni / imāmi tu gṛhameva durgatidvārapidhānāt / dhanopamāni āryasaptadhanāni, alpecchatā, saṃtoṣaśca / mitravat tridhātuprayogaṃ kurvannapi nirvāṇāśayatā, vipuladāne 'pi vipākanirapekṣatā, sarvadharmānutpādajñāne 'pi karmavipākānutsargaḥ, sarvadharmanairātmyajñāne 'pi sattveṣu karuṇotpādaḥ / mūlasamāḥ śraddhā, śravaṇaṃ, tyāgaḥ , kṣāntiśca / kṣetropamaṃ śīlam / bandhusamāḥ daśapāramitāḥ / ācāryopamāstu ṣaḍanusmṛtayaḥ / upādhyāyopamāstu āryakāśyapa-paripṛcchāsūtre bodhicittāvismaraṇāya catvāro dharmāḥ / śreṣṭhisamāḥ śikṣāsamuccaye caturdaśāpakārapratipakṣāḥ / bhaginīsamāni caturapramāṇāni /
body.translated_text: Just as beings are attached to their breath and depend upon it, so too <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are attached to and depend upon <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), which is comparable to the breath of life. The <s>Dharma</s> comparable to parents is <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion). Without their arising, the emergence of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is impossible. Like a housewife, (one should) meet three times daily and nightly with the perceptions of death, training, and the accumulation of <s>karma</s>. Like a house, the ten wholesome actions (serve as protection) — indeed, these are the very house, because they bar the door to lower rebirths. Comparable to wealth are the seven noble riches (<s>āryasaptadhana</s>): having few desires and contentment. Like a friend, even while engaging with the three realms, one maintains the aspiration for <s>Nirvāṇa</s>; even in abundant generosity, one has no regard for its fruits; even while knowing the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>, one does not abandon the (law of) <s>karma</s> and its results; even while knowing the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, one generates compassion for beings. Comparable to roots are faith, hearing (the teachings), generosity, and patience. Comparable to a field is <s>śīla</s> (moral discipline). Comparable to relatives are the ten <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). Comparable to a teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) are the six <s>anusmṛtis</s> (recollections). Comparable to a preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>) are the four <s>dharmas</s> for not forgetting <s>bodhicitta</s> as stated in the <s>Āryakāśyapaparipṛcchāsūtra</s>. Comparable to a merchant are the fourteen antidotes to harm in the <s>Śikṣāsamuccaya</s>. Comparable to a sister are the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>).

body.text: dāsopamāni catuḥsaṃgrahavastūni / prajopamastu śva-dāsa-cāṇḍālavadahaṅkāra-nāśaḥ / netropame tu āśayādhyāśayaviśuddhī / dhātrīsamaṃ kalyāṇamitram / rājopamaṃ triratnam / toyasaṃkāropamā trimaṇḍalapariśuddhiḥ / mārgadarśakasamāḥ smṛti-samprajanya-yoniśomanasikārāpramādāḥ, caturviparyāsapratipakṣasevanañca / carrnavat sattvāparityāgānugrahau / alaṅkāropamāḥ śraddhā, śīlaṃ, tyāgaḥ, śrutaṃ, prajñā ca / vyādhipīḍopamaṃ tu ādhyātmikabāhyavastvabhiniviṣṭacittam / hatacittapuruṣavat gṛhastho bodhisattva evaṃ vicārayati- kadāhaṃ brahmacārī bhaveyam / pravrajita evaṃ cintayati- kadāhaṃ jagato duḥkhāni moktuṃ kṣama iti / kusīdopamaṃ gṛhasthena kṣetrādīnām aparityāgaḥ / pravrajitena dauḥśīlyādīnāmaprahāṇam / śīlaskandhasūtre- 'bhikṣavaḥ, pravrajitena hastiyuddhadarśanamapi mithyājīva iti uktam /
body.translated_text: Comparable to a servant are the four means of gathering disciples (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>). Comparable to offspring is the destruction of ego like a dog, a servant, or an outcaste. Comparable to eyes are the purity of intention (<s>āśaya</s>) and higher intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>). Comparable to a wet-nurse is a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>). Comparable to a king is the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels). Comparable to a drainage channel is the purity of the three spheres (<s>trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi</s>). Comparable to a guide are mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), clear comprehension (<s>samprajanya</s>), proper mental engagement (<s>yoniśomanasikāra</s>), and vigilance (<s>apramāda</s>), as well as the practice of antidotes to the four distortions (<s>viparyāsa</s>). Like feet, (one should practice) non-abandonment and benefiting of beings. Comparable to ornaments are faith, moral discipline, generosity, learning, and wisdom. Comparable to affliction by disease is a mind fixated on internal and external objects. Like a person whose spirit is crushed, a householder <s>Bodhisattva</s> reflects thus: "When shall I become a celibate practitioner?" A renunciant reflects thus: "When shall I be able to liberate the world from sufferings?" Comparable to sloth is a householder's non-renunciation of fields and the like, and a renunciant's non-abandonment of moral laxity and the like. In the <s>Śīlaskandhasūtra</s>, it is said: "O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), for a renunciant, even watching an elephant fight is wrong livelihood."

body.text: susvabhāvopamo yoniśomanasikāravān / mūkopamaḥ paradoṣa-bhrāntyanākhyātā, svaguṇānākhyātā, aparanindakaśca / andhopamo 'paradoṣadraṣṭā / gṛhītacauropamaḥ saddharmavināśe saddharmagrāhakaḥ / bālopamaḥ suvāk, sphūrtimān, sukhadaḥ, sutoṣaḥ, supoṣaḥ, subharaḥ, santuṣṭaśca / dūtopamastu bodhisattvo bahvartho bahukriya udāracittaśca / amātyopamo dṛḍhapratijñaḥ / paṇḍitopamo 'pratihatasattvaḥ pratyupakārī ca / śiṣyopamastu trirdivā triśca rātrau guruparyupāsakaḥ, kṛtapuṇyasambhārasañcayaḥ saṃvarapoṣakaśca / pratyutthāpakopamaḥ sarvasattvabuddhatvaprāpaṇapūrvam svabuddhatvakāmaḥ / andhanāyakopamaḥ svabuddhabhāvapūrva parārthakriyāḥ / prathamakalpamanuṣyopama ācaraṇa-śīla-jīvikā-vidhi-dṛṣṭisampannaḥ / sakāmapuruṣopamaḥ samastacaryāpathaparārthapariṇāmanaḥ, yathā- 'āryaratnameghasūtroktam' / andhakāropamo mahāmadhyamakārthanityavāsaḥ / ghātakopamastyaktamithyādṛṣṭyutpādaḥ / cauropamaḥ tyaktapramādānādaraḥ / śatrūpamastu ahrīpramādaḥ / mūrkhopamaḥ smṛti-samprajanyavirahitaḥ / mattopamaḥ catuḥkṛṣṇaḥ / tiryagupamo 'jñātaśikṣānayaḥ / vadhikopamo niṣkaruṇācāraḥ / akṛtajñopamastyaktaprātimokṣasaṃvaraḥ / anāthopama upāyakauśalyarahitaḥ / unmattopamaḥ kāryākāryānabhijñatā /
body.translated_text: [A <s>Bodhisattva</s>] is like one of good nature (<s>susvabhāvopama</s>): possessing proper mental attention (<s>yoniśomanasikāra</s>). Like a mute (<s>mūkopama</s>): not declaring others' faults and errors, not declaring one's own virtues, and not blaming others. Like a blind person (<s>andhopama</s>): not seeing others' faults. Like a captured thief (<s>gṛhītacauropama</s>): upholding the true <s>Dharma</s> when the true <s>Dharma</s> is being destroyed. Like a child (<s>bālopama</s>): of pleasant speech, energetic, happiness-giving, easily pleased, easily nourished, easy to support, and contented. Like a messenger (<s>dūtopama</s>): the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is of great purpose, many activities, and noble mind. Like a minister (<s>amātyopama</s>): firm in resolve. Like a wise person (<s>paṇḍitopama</s>): of unobstructed energy and reciprocating kindness. Like a student (<s>śiṣyopama</s>): attending the teacher three times during the day and three times at night, having accumulated the collection of merit, and nourishing the vows. Like one who uplifts (<s>pratyutthāpakopama</s>): desiring one's own <s>Buddhahood</s> only after leading all beings to <s>Buddhahood</s>. Like a guide for the blind (<s>andhanāyakopama</s>): performing acts for the benefit of others, preceded by one's own attainment of <s>Buddhahood</s>. Like a person of the first age (<s>prathamakalpamanuṣyopama</s>): endowed with right conduct, morality, livelihood, method, and view. Like a person who has fulfilled his desires (<s>sakāmapuruṣopama</s>): transforming the entire path of conduct for the benefit of others, as stated in the <s>Āryaratnameghasūtra</s>. Like darkness (<s>andhakāropama</s>): permanently dwelling in the meaning of the great <s>Madhyamaka</s>. Like a slayer (<s>ghātakopama</s>): having destroyed the arising of wrong views. Like a thief (<s>cauropama</s>): having stolen away heedlessness and negligence. [Conversely,] like an enemy (<s>śatrūpama</s>) [are] shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>). Like a fool (<s>mūrkhopama</s>): one devoid of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) and <s>samprajanya</s> (clear comprehension). Like a drunkard (<s>mattopama</s>): one possessing the four black <s>dharmas</s>. Like an animal (<s>tiryagupama</s>): one who does not know the method of training. Like an executioner (<s>vadhikopama</s>): one whose conduct is without compassion. Like an ingrate (<s>akṛtajñopama</s>): one who has abandoned the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> discipline. Like a destitute person (<s>anāthopama</s>): one devoid of <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means). Like a madman (<s>unmattopama</s>): not knowing what should and should not be done.

body.text: mārābhibhūtopamaḥ pañca-pañcāśad-dvātriṃśadāntarāyikadharmāmabhijñatā / ke ca (te) pañcapañcāśad? 'āryabodhisattvapiṭake' tadyathā- āntarāyika eko dharmaḥ- pramādaḥ / āntarāyikau dvau dharmau-ahrīkyam anapatrāpyañca / trayaḥ- rāgo dveṣo mohaśca / catvāraḥ- catasraḥ asadgatayaḥ / pañcaprāṇātipāto 'dattādānam kāmamithyācāro mṛṣāvādo madyapānaṃ ca / ṣaḍ-buddha-dharma-saṃgha-śīla-ācārya-jyeṣṭhānādaraḥ / sapta- saptavidhā mānāḥ / aṣṭau-mithyāṣṭakam / nava- navadhā cittāghātavastūni / daśa- daśākuśalāni iti prāptam /
body.translated_text: Like one overcome by <s>Māra</s> (<s>mārābhibhūtopama</s>): not knowing the fifty-five and thirty-two obstacle-<s>dharmas</s>. And what are those fifty-five? In the <s>Āryabodhisattvapiṭaka</s>, they are as follows: One obstacle-<s>dharma</s>: heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>). Two obstacle-<s>dharmas</s>: shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>). Three: passion (<s>rāga</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>). Four: the four bad destinations (<s>asadgati</s>). Five: killing (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>), stealing (<s>adattādāna</s>), sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>), false speech (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>), and drinking intoxicants (<s>madyapāna</s>). Six: disrespect for the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Saṃgha</s>, morality, teacher, and elders. Seven: the seven types of pride (<s>māna</s>). Eight: the eightfold wrong path (<s>mithyāṣṭaka</s>). Nine: the nine grounds for mental affliction (<s>cittāghātavastu</s>). Ten: the ten unwholesome actions (<s>daśākuśala</s>) — thus the total [of fifty-five] is reached.

body.text: dvātriṃśad āntarāyikā dharmā api 'āryamahāyānopadeśasūtre' tadyathā- 'putri! mahāyānāntarāyikā dharmāstu dvātriṃśat / tairāntarāyikaiḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ śīghraṃ na niryāṇaṃ bhavati / ke ca dvātriṃśat? tadyathā- śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānakāmitā, indrabrahmatvakāmitā, janmasaṃsthabrahmacaryam, kuśalamūlaikarāgaḥ, bhogasampatmātsaryam, sattvaviṣamadānam, śīlaśaithilyam, paracittārakṣaṇam, vyāpāda-pratighānuśayaḥ, taccittalayaḥ, muṣitasmṛtitā, śravaṇānarthikatā, avicāraṇā, anāryacaryā, mānātimānavivṛddhiḥ, kāya-vāk-citta-karmāpariśuddhiḥ, saddharmāparirakṣaṇam, ācāryadharmapraticchādanam, saṃgrahavastūtsargaḥ, sammodanīyadharmatyāgaḥ, pāpamitrasevanam, bodhyapariṇāmaneti triskandhavipakṣatā, alpakuśalamūlamanyanā, anupāyapatitabuddhiḥ, parāṅmukhībhūya triratnāśaṃsanam, bodhisattvavyāpādacintanam / aśrutadharmaprahāṇam, mārakarmānavabodhaḥ, lokāyatamantragrahaṇam, sattvāparipācanam, saṃsārādaparikheda', iti /
body.translated_text: The thirty-two obstacle-<s>dharmas</s> are also [stated] in the <s>Āryamahāyānopadeśasūtra</s>, as follows: 'O daughter! There are thirty-two <s>dharmas</s> that are obstacles to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Through those obstacles, there is no swift progress toward omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>). And what are the thirty-two? They are as follows: (1) desire for the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles, (2) desire to become <s>Indra</s> or <s>Brahmā</s>, (3) celibacy lasting only a single lifetime, (4) attachment to a single root of merit, (5) miserliness regarding wealth and prosperity, (6) unequal giving to beings, (7) laxity in morality, (8) not protecting others' minds, (9) latent tendencies of ill-will and aversion, (10) sinking of the mind regarding those, (11) lost mindfulness, (12) disinterest in hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, (13) non-investigation, (14) ignoble conduct, (15) growth of pride (<s>māna</s>) and excessive pride (<s>atimāna</s>), (16) impurity of actions of body, speech, and mind, (17) not protecting the true <s>Dharma</s>, (18) concealing the teacher's <s>Dharma</s>, (19) abandoning the means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), (20) abandoning the <s>dharma</s> of friendly discourse, (21) associating with evil friends (<s>pāpamitra</s>), (22) non-dedication to awakening, (23) opposition to the three aggregates [of virtue] (<s>triskandha</s>), (24) considering small roots of merit as sufficient, (25) intelligence that has fallen into wrong methods, (26) turning away yet expecting rewards from the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels), (27) thinking with ill-will toward <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, (28) abandoning unheard <s>dharmas</s>, (29) not understanding the activities of <s>Māra</s>, (30) taking up worldly materialist mantras (<s>lokāyata</s>), (31) not maturing beings, (32) not being wearied of <s>saṃsāra</s>.'

body.text:
'putri! dvātriṃśad ime mahāyānasya āntarāyikāḥ samyak vyapadiṣṭāḥ / tairantarāyaiḥ sarvajñatā' niḥsaraṇam / kiṃ tarhi? tathāpi putri, yāvanto hi mahāyānaguṇā antarāyā api tāvantastāvad ityuktam / api ca, aprameyā antarāyadharmā bahuṣu sūtreṣu dṛśyante, kintu atra granthagauravāt na nirupyante / etanmārgasthīkṛtādikarmikabodhisattvaistattatsūtreṣu draṣṭavyam, āsthitaye ca prayatitavyam /'
aparāṇyapi sāṃkathyāni bahūni vartante-sughoraparuṣaṃ suduḥsahaṃ dukhaṃ ciraṃ sahyata idamapi mahadāścaryam / caturoghavikṣiptaṃ paunaḥpunyena kaṅkālayānārohaṇaṃ tadapi mahadāścaryam / bhāryā gṛhaṃ ca prahāya suvratādāne 'pi sadā kāyavāṅmanovikṣepa idamapi mahadāścaryam / svalpamātrasyāpi kuśalamūlasya abhāve 'pi tasyaivārthato buddhajñānagaveṣaṇam idamapi mahadāścaryam pratimokṣaśikṣābhāve 'pi- mahāyānaśreṣṭhabodhidvayagaveṣaṇam idamapi mahadāścaryam / ityādiṣu mahāścaryeṣu bahuṣvapi satsu, jambūdvīpapuruṣasya vikalpācārāḥ kathaṃ vaktuṃ śakyante / tasmād bhavanto muktikāmā vidvāṃsastairunmattaiḥ saha akṛtasaṃsargā apramattās tiṣṭhantu / evaṃ te karuṇāviṣayatvavyatiriktāḥ uttamamārgavyapadeśe 'pi tatra na praviśanti, kimahaṃ karavāṇi / yāvad abhijñatā na prāpyate tāvad anyeṣāṃ vipākāsaṃbhavāt khaḍgavat sthātavyam / sadgururgaveṣaṇīyaḥ, sadā sūtrāṇi ca draṣṭavyāni /
body.translated_text:
'O daughter! These thirty-two obstacles to the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) have been properly enumerated. Through those obstacles, escape to <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) [is blocked]. What then? Nevertheless, O daughter, as many as are the qualities of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, so many are the obstacles—thus it has been said. Moreover, immeasurable obstacle-<s>dharmas</s> are seen in many <s>sūtras</s>, but here they are not examined due to the weightiness of the text. Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are beginners established on this path should examine them in the respective <s>sūtras</s> and strive to adhere to them.'
There are also many other discussions—that extremely harsh and unbearable suffering is endured for a long time, this too is a great wonder. That one tossed about by the four floods repeatedly mounts the skeleton-vehicle, that too is a great wonder. That having abandoned wife and home, even in the undertaking of good vows there is always distraction of body, speech, and mind, this too is a great wonder. That even in the absence of even a small amount of <s>kuśalamūla</s> (roots of merit), one still seeks <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge for that very purpose, this too is a great wonder. That even in the absence of <s>prātimokṣa</s> (monastic discipline) training, one seeks the supreme pair of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, this too is a great wonder. And so on—even though there are many such great wonders, how can the conceptual practices of a person of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> be expressed? Therefore, let the learned ones who desire liberation remain without association with those madmen, and remain vigilant. Thus those, being beyond the scope of compassion, even when the supreme path is taught, do not enter into it—what can I do? Until <s>abhijñā</s> (direct knowledge) is attained, since the ripening of others is not possible, one should remain like a rhinoceros. A true <s>guru</s> should be sought, and the <s>sūtras</s> should always be studied.
The <s>Sūtrasamuccayopadeśa</s> (Instruction on the Compendium of Sūtra Meanings), composed by the great learned <s>ācārya</s> <s>Dīpaṅkaraśrījñāna</s>, is complete.

body.text: tenaiva bhāratīyamahopādhyāyena mahāsaṃśodhakalokacakṣuṣā jayaśīlena (chul khrimas rgyal va) ca anūdya sampādya ca nirṇītaḥ //
body.translated_text: It was translated, edited, and finalized by that same Indian great <s>upādhyāya</s> (preceptor) and by the great redactor, the eye of the world, <s>Jayaśīla</s> (chul khrims rgyal ba).
